head: pr17399-r3
report:
I found two defects you should fix before merging. Both come from where the patch puts the hold: it waits after state the request has already locked in, which is a cross-process lease or a SigV4 signature. Each one below was reproduced with a probe that calls the real production functions. ## 1. Stop holding the provider in-flight lease while paused (P1) **File:** `packages/ai/src/stream.ts:690-701`, in `withProviderInFlightLimit` **Mechanism.** The patch takes the cross-process in-flight slot first (`acquireProviderInFlightSlot`, a filesystem lease that keeps sending a heartbeat). Only after that does it wait on the hold (`await holdBeforeDispatch(hold, options?.signal)`). The comment calls this order deliberate ("Last, so the slot wait above cannot outlast it"). `/pause` only pauses the process that engaged it, but the lease directory is shared by every omp process on the host. A paused process therefore keeps its slot for as long as a person leaves it paused, and any other unpaused omp process using that provider with `maxInFlightRequests` / `providers.

.maxConcurrency` waits that whole time. Before this patch, side requests had no hold at all, and the agent loop checked the gate before entering the stream, so a paused process held no lease. This happens on every path that now passes `agentPauseGate.dispatchHold(...)`: compaction, memories, commit messages, judges, side turns and others. It also happens when the agent loop's own hold fires after the gate check, for example during credential resolution. **Trigger.** Run two processes against one lease root with limit 1: - Process A engages `agentPauseGate.pause()` and calls `streamSimple(..., { maxInFlightRequests: { tests: 1 }, beforeDispatch: agentPauseGate.dispatchHold() })`. - Process B, which is not paused, calls `streamSimple` with the same limit. **Measured.** Probe is `scratch/.../r2/lease-child.ts`, which imports the snapshot's `ai/src/stream.ts` and `agent/src/pause.ts`: ``` $ bun lease-child.ts A leaseroot & sleep 1.5; bun lease-child.ts B leaseroot A paused; lease dir entries: ["WYMOvDpBhBEFZr8aKQ0IRz39y9SSzkmLFM0aXi-i5EE",".../943064-1793343106686-.../info.json"] B result: STILL WAITING after 5000ms (+5010ms) # control: B alone on a fresh root $ bun lease-child.ts B leaseroot2 B DISPATCHED at +144ms B result: done (+151ms) ``` **Possible fix.** Wait on the hold before acquiring the slot. Then either check the hold again after acquiring and release the lease if the gate is closed, or release the lease for the duration of any park. ## 2. Don't send a paused Bedrock retry with its pre-pause SigV4 signature (P1) **File:** `packages/ai/src/providers/amazon-bedrock.ts:280-318`, where `signRequest` runs once and then `fetchWithRetry(..., fetch: options.fetch)` is called. The hold that fires is `packages/ai/src/utils/transport-fetch.ts:182` (`await holdAllBeforeDispatch(holds, signal)` inside the built fetch). **Mechanism.** `sendBedrockRequest` computes `x-amz-date` and `authorization` once, before it calls `fetchWithRetry`. The patch puts the hold inside the transport fetch so that "the attempts a provider retries itself" wait out `/pause`. A retry that parks there is sent after resume with the old headers. AWS rejects SigV4 requests whose `x-amz-date` is more than 5 minutes off the server clock. That limit is documented AWS behaviour; I did not call AWS. So any pause longer than 5 minutes turns a retryable 429/503 into an auth failure once the user resumes. The same order exists in `bedrock-mantle.ts:39-59`. There, `createSignedFetch` signs and then calls the held `baseFetch`. A `/pause` that starts during the credential lookup gives the same result. **Trigger.** 1. Stream a `bedrock-converse-stream` model with `AWS_BEDROCK_SKIP_AUTH=1`, `maxHttpAttempts: 3` and `beforeDispatch: agentPauseGate.dispatchHold()`. 2. Make the first attempt engage `/pause` and return 503. 3. Move the clock forward 10 minutes, then resume. **Measured.** Probe is `scratch/.../r2/sigv4-hold.test.ts`: ``` $ cd packages/ai && bun test .../r2/sigv4-hold.test.ts attempts on wire while paused: 1 attempt 1: x-amz-date=20261030T065321Z sent=2026-10-30T06:53:21.327Z signature age=0s attempt 2: x-amz-date=20261030T065321Z sent=2026-10-30T07:03:24.329Z signature age=603s error: expect(received).toBeLessThan(expected) Expected: < 300 Received: 603.329 ``` **Not measured: Vertex.** `createVertexAuthenticatedFetch` (`stream.ts:742-743`) probably has the same problem with a longer limit. It gets the access token, then calls the held `baseFetch`, so a pause longer than the token's lifetime (about 1 hour) would send an expired bearer token. To settle it, run the same probe against `google-vertex` with a token mock that has a short expiry. **Possible fix.** Sign or mint the credential after the hold. That means calling the hold before `signRequest` / `getVertexAccessToken` on every attempt, or re-signing inside the retry callback. --- **Verdict:** not safe to merge. While paused, a process blocks other processes' provider slots indefinitely, and on Bedrock any pause over 5 minutes makes the retries it held fail authentication after resume.
